title: Boolean algebra rules
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Normalise 0.0110 × 2⁴ using a two’s-complement mantissa. Give the new mantissa and exponent.
questions.feedback: Shift the mantissa one place left and decrease the exponent by one to preserve the value. A normalised positive two’s-complement mantissa begins 01 ; a negative one begins 10 .

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: A sorted array is [3, 8, 12, 19, 27, 35, 42] . When searching for 27 , which indexes are checked, in order?
questions.feedback: Binary search tests the middle index of the remaining sorted range, using zero-based indexing.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Show the array after one full left-to-right pass of ascending bubble sort on [7, 3, 5, 2] .
questions.feedback: Compare adjacent values and swap when the left value is larger. The largest value, 7, moves to the end.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: An alarm sounds if the door is open AND the system is armed, OR if panic is pressed. Write Q using A, B and C.
questions.feedback: A = door open, B = armed, C = panic pressed. Group door AND armed first; panic is an alternative trigger.

blocks.title: De Morgan
blocks.text: The operator inside the brackets swaps as each term is negated.

blocks.title: Distributive law
blocks.text: A appears in both groups. Write it once outside the brackets, then join B and C with OR. The matching OR form is also useful: (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C) = A ∨ (B ∧ C).

blocks.title: Association + commutation
blocks.text: These allow regrouping and reordering before other simplification.

questions.feedback: De Morgan — Rules for negating AND/OR groups.
